title: Reversing Valve Sensor Open
shortDescription: EcoNet detects open reversing valve solenoid circuit.
fullDescription: Ruud EcoNet heat pumps use a reversing valve solenoid energized in cooling mode. C7 indicates board cannot energize the valve or sense feedback.

causes.cause: Wire broken between board and valve

fixSteps.title: Ohm solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Should read ~10-30 ohms. Open = bad coil.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant system. EPA 608 required for valve replacement.

title: Defrost Cycle Active
shortDescription: Heat pump in defrost - melting outdoor coil ice.
fullDescription: Not an error. Outdoor unit reverses to cooling mode briefly, fan stops, aux heat may engage. Cycle ends when coil sensor warms.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Defrost lasts 5-10 minutes. Resumes heating after.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Defrost Stuck
shortDescription: Defrost cycle did not terminate within max time.
fullDescription: If outdoor coil sensor never warms, defrost can run >15 min, dumping cold air indoors and overworking aux heat.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate sensor clip on suction tube; check resistance per service chart.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Outdoor Air Sensor Fault
fullDescription: EcoNet uses outdoor air temp for staging and aux lockout. Sensor open or shorted disables smart staging.
symptoms: Aux heat runs more than usual

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor clipped near outdoor coil; check connector and resistance.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Reversing Valve Stuck
shortDescription: Valve will not shift between heat and cool.
fullDescription: Mechanical sticking of reversing valve slide. Common after long idle in one mode or low refrigerant charge.
symptoms: No mode change despite solenoid energized

fixSteps.title: Tap valve gently
fixSteps.instruction: Light rubber-mallet tap on valve body sometimes frees slide. Pro only.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Float Switch Open
fullDescription: Indoor air handler condensate pan filling because drain is clogged. Float switch interrupts Y to prevent water damage.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum drain
fixSteps.instruction: Wet/dry vac at outdoor drain termination for 30 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Flush with vinegar
fixSteps.instruction: Pour 1 cup distilled vinegar in cleanout tee.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Compressor Locked Rotor
shortDescription: Compressor failed to start - drawing locked-rotor amps.
fullDescription: Inverter or single-stage compressor cannot break free. Often capacitor or seized bearings.

fixSteps.title: Check capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge then test uF with meter; replace if >10% off-spec.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.
safetyWarning: Capacitor stores lethal charge. Discharge before touching.

title: High Discharge Temperature
fullDescription: Indicates low charge, restricted airflow, or failing compressor valves causing heat buildup.

fixSteps.title: Wash outdoor coil
fixSteps.instruction: Garden hose, fins from inside out.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Defrost Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor coil defrost thermistor invalid reading.
fullDescription: Defrost initiation depends on coil temp. Bad sensor causes either no defrost (icing) or constant defrost.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect, clean with electrical contact cleaner, reseat.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Loss of Communication Outdoor
shortDescription: EcoNet wall control lost link with outdoor unit.
fullDescription: Communicating system uses 1/2 data wires between indoor, outdoor, and thermostat. C2 specifically flags outdoor link failure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect bus
fixSteps.instruction: Check 1/2/R/C at outdoor terminal block for tightness.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: High Pressure Trip
fullDescription: Ruud heat pump code C5 indicates the high-pressure switch tripped, shutting down the compressor for protection.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
symptoms: Hot air not rejecting from coil
whenToCallPro: If trips repeat, fan capacitor or refrigerant charge needs a pro.

faq.a: Insufficient heat rejection from the outdoor coil.

title: Low Pressure Trip
fullDescription: Ruud heat pump C6 indicates suction pressure dropped below safe level, often from low refrigerant or restricted indoor airflow.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Filter Change
fixSteps.instruction: New filter; fan-only to thaw any ice.

whenToCallPro: Always indicates a leak; have it located and repaired.

title: Compressor Overload
fullDescription: C8 reports the compressor's internal thermal overload opened due to overheating or overcurrent.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
whenToCallPro: Repeated overload trips likely require pro diagnosis.

title: Voltage Out of Range
fullDescription: C9 indicates the heat pump detected line voltage too high or too low, shutting down for protection.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
symptoms: Unit shuts off during heat waves
whenToCallPro: Persistent voltage issues require electrician or utility involvement.

title: Outdoor Fan Capacitor
shortDescription: Outdoor fan capacitor weak or failed.
fullDescription: OFC indicates the outdoor fan capacitor is reading below spec, leading to slow or no fan startup.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
whenToCallPro: Capacitor work is electrical hazard - if uncomfortable, call a pro.

title: Compressor Run Capacitor
fullDescription: CFC indicates the compressor run capacitor is below spec, causing hard starts and overheating.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
whenToCallPro: Compressor caps are higher voltage - extra caution required; call pro if unsure.

faq.a: Only if you know capacitor handling.

title: Stuck Fan Motor
fullDescription: SFM means the outdoor fan motor is mechanically stuck despite power applied.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
whenToCallPro: For ECM fan motors, OEM replacement is required.

faq.a: Most modern motors are sealed - no lube possible.

title: TXV Restriction
fullDescription: TXV indicates the expansion valve is not metering correctly, often from contamination or failed power head.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
whenToCallPro: TXV replacement is a refrigerant-circuit job for a tech.

title: Defrost Relay Fault
fullDescription: DFR-v2 indicates the defrost board relay did not energize the reversing valve when commanded.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Listen
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for relay click during defrost.

whenToCallPro: Board replacement is straightforward but needs proper jumper settings.

faq.a: Yes if comfortable with low-voltage wiring.

title: Loss of Charge Protection
fullDescription: LSP triggers when the heat pump senses critical refrigerant loss to prevent compressor damage.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
whenToCallPro: Major leak requires complete service from a certified tech.

faq.a: Usually yes if leak is found.
Sometimes needed if leak is in evap.

title: High Pressure Switch Trip
fullDescription: Ruud reports HPS when the high-pressure cutout switch trips.

title: Low Pressure Switch Trip
fullDescription: LPS indicates suction-side pressure dropped below the cutout — refrigerant leak likely.

title: Discharge Temperature Sensor Fault
fullDescription: DTS means the discharge temp sensor is reading out of range.

title: Suction Temperature Sensor Fault
fullDescription: STS reports the suction-line sensor is open/shorted; superheat calc disabled.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault
fullDescription: CTS indicates the outdoor coil thermistor failed.

title: Compressor Lockout
fullDescription: CLO is a 24-hour lockout state after repeated compressor protection trips.

title: Compressor Control Tripped
fullDescription: CCT reports the CoreSense / compressor protection module saw a fault.

title: EcoNet Bus Loss
fullDescription: EBL means the outdoor EcoNet board lost the comm bus to the thermostat.

faq.a: Some EcoNet outdoor units don't fall back.

title: Inverter Fault
fullDescription: INV groups variable-speed compressor inverter faults — overcurrent, over-temp, bus voltage.

title: Aux Heat Lockout
fullDescription: AUX lockout occurs when EcoNet detects aux heat strip current draw outside spec, or sequencer fault.

fixSteps.title: Reset Limit
fixSteps.instruction: Press red button on high-limit switch.

faq.a: Yes — but no aux below balance point.

safetyWarning: 240V at heat strips even with thermostat off.

title: AC1 — Inverter Drive Comm Loss
shortDescription: Outdoor lost CAN-bus to inverter drive.
fullDescription: Ruud Endeavor inverter heat pumps share Rheem platform - AC1 = CAN packets stopped >5 sec.

title: AC2 — Compressor Drive Overcurrent
fullDescription: AC2 = inverter overcurrent on Ruud Endeavor.

title: HPS — High Pressure Switch Trip
fullDescription: Ruud HPS code = high pressure cutout. Fan/coil/charge.

title: LPS — Low Pressure Switch Trip
fullDescription: Ruud LPS code = low pressure cutout.

title: DTH — Discharge Temperature High
fullDescription: Ruud DTH protects compressor at over-temp.

title: BRN — Brownout Lockout
fullDescription: Ruud BRN = brownout protection.

title: HLO — Hard Lockout
fullDescription: Ruud HLO = compressor locked, manual reset.

title: CCH — Crankcase Heater Open
fullDescription: Ruud CCH on inverter units = open crankcase heater. Risk of flood-back.

title: LLS — Liquid Line Sensor Open
fullDescription: Ruud LLS = liquid sensor used for charge calc is open/shorted.

title: ECN — EcoNet Comm Loss
fullDescription: Ruud ECN = EcoNet 4-wire bus failure.
